pr_title: Improve docs around run rerun job flag
pr_body: ### Description This PR fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/7507. In the linked issue, there was confusion around which `id` to provide to `run rerun --job `. Due to legacy reasons, this `job_id` is **not** the one you would expect simply by taking the suffix of the URL in the browser when navigating to a job. This PR adds documentation to the `Long` description of the `rerun` command to draw attention to this, and how to find IDs for jobs in a run. ### Reviewer Notes Here is a screenshot of the new text in `help` and in the `manual` (I'm not sure how to open manpages for a local build):
pr_comments: @taha-au do you think this would have helped you? Is there anything you think might be missing?

issue_context.title: `gh run rerun` with job ID doesn't work
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Attempting to rerun a job with the job ID (as shown in the `.../actions/runs/<run-ID>/job/<job-ID>` URL) using the `gh run rerun -j <job-ID>` command throws a 404 error no matter the token used. However, `gh run rerun <run-ID>` works as expected.

CLI info:
```
gh version 2.20.0 (2022-11-08)
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Type `gh run rerun -j <job-ID>` with any valid job ID
2. See error: `failed to get job: HTTP 404: Not Found (https://api.github.com/repos/superblocksteam/superblocks/actions/jobs/<job-ID>)`

### Expected vs actual behavior

I expect the rerun of the job to work, but what actually happens is that I get a 404. 

It is also unclear why specifying a run ID and a job ID (which exists in the run) together aren't valid - `gh run rerun <run-ID> -j <job-ID>`.

### Logs

```
❯ gh --version
gh version 2.29.0 (2023-05-10)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v2.29.0

❯ gh run view 5107576769 --json jobs | jq -r '.jobs[] | select(.name == "allow-merge") | .url | capture("/jobs/(?<job_id>[^/]+)$") | .job_id'
9180945000

❯ gh run rerun -j 9180945000
failed to get job: HTTP 404: Not Found (https://api.github.com/repos/superblocksteam/superblocks/actions/jobs/9180945000)
```

Run and job IDs together:
```
❯ gh run rerun 5107576769 --job 9180945000
specify only one of `<run-id>` or `--job`

Usage:  gh run rerun [<run-id>] [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --debug        Rerun with debug logging
      --failed       Rerun only failed jobs, including dependencies
  -j, --job string   Rerun a specific job from a run, including dependencies
```
comments: Hi @taha-au, thanks for the report. Although I'm not that familiar with this CLI command or the backing API, I do see the same behaviour and I would expect it to work. I'll keep looking into this today. Cheers.

Hi @taha-au, I took a bit more time to look at the `JOB_ID` that is expected on the [`Get a job for a workflow run` endpoint](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-jobs?apiVersion=2022-11-28#get-a-job-for-a-workflow-run). When I checked `gh run view <RUN_ID>`, I noticed that there was a `databaseId` field



```
cli git:(status-tests) ✗ gh run view 5069618997 --json jobs
{
  "jobs": [
    {
      "completedAt": "2023-05-30T12:28:41Z",
      "conclusion": "success",
      "databaseId": 13859194509,
      ...
      "url": "https://github.com/cli/cli/actions/runs/5069618997/jobs/9210977364"
  ]
}
```

This can be selected with:

```
gh run view 5069618997 --json jobs --jq '.jobs[0].databaseId'
13859194509
```

When I put this into the `gh run rerun` it seems to work as expected:

```
➜  cli git:(status-tests) ✗ gh run rerun -j 13859194509
✓ Requested rerun of job 13859194509 on run 5069618997
```

I think that this `-j` flag represents some `databaseID` rather than the ID suffix of the URL explains why you can't provide a `RUN_ID` and `JOB_ID` as arguments because they represent disparate concepts i.e. a `RUN_ID` and a `databaseID`. However, like you, I think this is **quite** confusing.

Before I follow up on on this confusion, it would be useful if you could try and repeat my steps from above and see whether it works for you. Thanks!

Hey @taha-au, I did a little more digging and it seems like we modify the raw API response from `/repos/cli/cli/actions/runs/5069618997/jobs`. That response looks like this:

```
{
  "total_count": 1,
  "jobs": [
    {
      "id": 13861680344,
      "run_id": 5069618997,
      ...
      "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/cli/cli/actions/jobs/13861680344",
      "html_url": "https://github.com/cli/cli/actions/runs/5069618997/jobs/9211162426",
      ...
```

And we seem to take this `id` and rename it `databaseId` and we rename the `html_url` as `url`. This was requested by Mislav in [this comment](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/6120#issuecomment-1289177962). With this context, it's a bit clearer why the `databaseID` is the correct id to use for programmatic access because in the original payload it represented `jobs[].id` in the JSON structure. 

I asked internally why the `html_url` has what seems to be an unrelated suffix and the answer is that there is a historical mismatch between "Actions Jobs" and "Checks" and the team is aware of it.

Therefore, I'd ask that you try the instructions above (repeated here):

```
gh run rerun -j $(gh run view <RUN_ID> --json jobs --jq '.jobs[0].databaseId')
```

yep that worked! thanks for the help ❤️ 

as I hope you agree, none of this is obvious in the CLI directly or in the public docs for rerunning jobs in a workflow run. could we please update the relevant documentation, and provide a reference recipe there (as you've given me in your reply) for how to find this "job ID"?

https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs?apiVersion=2022-11-28#re-run-a-job-from-a-workflow-run
https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_run_rerun

It would be a good idea to update the docs around this. I got bitten a million times already by thinking that the last number in a browser URL for an Actions job is a job ID and that somehow isn't true 😭 

Thanks @williammartin for thorough research.
I'm going to close this as fixed by #7527, if you feel we're missing something in the new docs @taha-au, please let us know. Thanks!

review_comments: This invocation could be made shorter for clarity. If the goal is to demonstrate programmatic access to job IDs, then `gh run view <run-id> --json jobs` would suffice (with extracting the `databaseId` being left as an exercise to the reader). If the goal could be satisfied by seeing job IDs in human-readable format, then note that `gh run view <run-id>` prints them as well.

I'm happy to change this if you feel strongly but I think it needs to be explained that the field called `databaseId` is the one the user should be looking for. `databaseId` isn't a concept that exists in the API and doesn't link to being a `job-id`. Having it in the command seems as useful as a wordy explanation to me.
